claims.quote: Folded on top was a leather book, soft at the corners and stained with a child's economy of ink. The cover had no title, only a loop of string that had been slipped through itself for a fast, private binding. I sat on an upturned crate and opened it.
claims.value: in loc-attic on top of obj-locked-trunk under tarp

claims.quote: Handwriting filled the first half of the journal: small, slanted, with a careful unevenness that belonged to anyone who had practiced saying the same secret over and over.
claims.value: child's handwriting, small slanted, careful unevenness

claims.quote: The journal held a recipe more than a confession. I copied the lines into my head and read them back because they hurt in a useful way. They were literal and terrible.
claims.value: contains a literal ritual to be performed at shallow well in loc-basement using the lullaby and brass key

claims.quote:
"Sing the lullaby at the well, and name it true.

1. Bring the lullaby to the shallow well in the basement.
2. Wind the box until its key will not turn again; let the tune sit in the stone.
3. Lay the brass key on the lip, say what was done, and drop your eyes."
claims.value: 1) bring lullaby to the well; 2) wind the box until key will not turn again; 3) lay brass key on well lip, say what was done, drop eyes

claims.quote: Beneath the instructions, in the same small hand, a single line sat like a signature: "Cost: there will be a price."
So the book named a place and an action and a price. It also named someone who wanted the telling to be true.
claims.value: attributed to Margaret (char-margaret-ghost) by signature in journal

claims.quote: The brass key had been tucked into the back pages. It was warm as if someone had just closed their fist around it; the shaft bore a nick like a small tooth.
claims.value: tucked into back pages of obj-journal in loc-attic; warm; shaft has a nick

claims.quote: Up close the head of the key looked cut to the trunk's lock — the nick mirrored the roughness of the hole in the attic floor — and I could tell, by the way it sat in my palm, that it would likely fit the lock cleanly if I turned it there.
claims.value: physically fits obj-locked-trunk; likely to turn cleanly

claims.quote: The line I said made the glass go thin. In the mirror the attic changed: light softened to a warm dust, the trunks wore old cloth and, by the trunk I had just moved, a child sat with bare knees and a hair ribbon.
claims.value: mirror shows displaced reflection when narrator speaks aloud (reading the journal) or when music box plays; reflection is of attic as it was with a child present

claims.quote: The movement in the reflection matched the notes that were threading up through the floorboards; first a hairsbreadth of latency, then perfect alignment, like a clock catching itself.
claims.value: mirror's replay synchronises with obj-music-box sound with slight latency then exact alignment

claims.quote:
"1. Bring the lullaby to the shallow well in the basement.
2. Wind the box until its key will not turn again; let the tune sit in the stone."
claims.value: music box's tune (the lullaby) must be brought to the well and wound until it cannot turn further as part of ritual

claims.quote: There is a bluntness to children's writing when a thing matters. I could feel, in the margin flourishes and the sudden adult hush of step‑instructions, the person who had written it — patient, careful, wanting a witness with rules.
claims.value: char-margaret-ghost's voice: patient, careful, childlike turning suddenly formal; fixated on being witnessed for how she died

claims.quote: I tightened my fingers on the key and, because the house had begun to call the past forward, I put the journal under my arm and climbed down to the stairs, the sound of the lullaby falling ahead of me through the house.
claims.value: takes obj-journal and obj-brass-key from attic and moves toward basement (intention to act on ritual)
